newsitem.title: CROATIA: PLIVA JUMPS TO NEW HIGH ON CROATIA BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: PLIVA JUMPS TO NEW HIGH ON CROATIA BOURSE.

text.p: Drugs concern Pliva jumped to a new all-time high on Croatia's central bourse on Thursday, hitting 600 kuna in mid-session.
"Pliva sold more than 7,000 shares (by 1030 GMT), of which 1,282 went for 600 kuna," Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage said.
The stock broke through all-time highs several times last month and had another record-breaking session on Wednesday, closing at 584 kuna.
Nikolac said Pliva opened at 575 kuna to rise gradually to 600 kuna but retreated to 592 around 1030 GMT.
Its Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) climbed to $18 in London, up from $17.6 at the open.
"The stronger dollar has definitely contributed to the rise in Pliva's price...but the whole market is generally in a very optimistic mood," Nikolac said.
Another quoted company, Zagrebacka Banka, which also set a new record of 2,500 kuna on Wednesday , had not traded by early afternoon on Thursday.
Buying orders for the bank fetched 2,585 kuna, while there were only two selling offers at 2,600 kuna, Nikolac said.
Its GDRs in London were also on the rise, climbing to $39.125 from $38.375 at opening. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
